headline: Medium pairwise risk: ComfyUI can feed untrusted image/workflow content into Rasa, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error paths; no direct shared-write or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can expose workflows and files, and Rasa ingests text/voice messages through chat channels. If ComfyUI output is copied into Rasa prompts or message content, attacker-controlled workflow text could steer dialogue. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this is inferred rather than observed, but uncertainty does not justify lowering it.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are pasted or forwarded into Rasa message text without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF an operator bridges the two through a shared chat or queue, Rasa may treat ComfyUI content as instructions.
mitigations: Add a strict content filter before any ComfyUI output reaches Rasa.
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from generated text.
Route only structured fields, not free-form text, between agents.
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like phrases before deployment.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model files locally, while Rasa handles text/voice and sends messages to allowlisted channels. No shared filesystem or authenticated workspace is documented, so direct leakage is not evidenced. The main risk is accidental copying of sensitive media into chat outputs, which is limited and avoidable.
conditions: IF operators manually move ComfyUI media into Rasa channels, those contents can leak to chat recipients.
IF Rasa is configured to echo attachments or transcripts, sensitive text may be exposed.
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI and Rasa on separate workspaces.
Disable attachment echoing in Rasa channels.
Redact sensitive metadata from images before handoff.
Use a manual review step before any media is shared externally.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI has no filesystem write, shell, or git modification capability, and Rasa only shows allowlisted network egress with no documented shared mutable resource. Without overlapping write access or a shared lockable resource, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible from the profiles provided.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo, conflict risk would emerge.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, concurrent updates could collide.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only with respect to shared assets.
Avoid placing them on the same writable workspace.
If shared state is added, require a lock or queue.
Audit any future permission changes before rollout.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa can treat upstream content as dialogue input, and ComfyUI can generate outputs that may be forwarded as text or metadata. If Rasa acts on ComfyUI-produced claims without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect customer responses. This is inferred from the profiles, not directly documented, so the higher medium level is appropriate.
conditions: IF ComfyUI-generated text is used as authoritative customer-support content, Rasa may repeat errors.
IF no verification step is inserted between generation and response, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review for any generated customer-facing text.
Add a verification prompt before Rasa sends a reply.
Limit ComfyUI output to non-authoritative suggestions.
Log source provenance for every handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. ComfyUI is offline-capable and Rasa shows only allowlisted egress, but neither profile states a compliance boundary that would create a breach by pairing them. With no evidence of a specific mismatch, the pathway is not established.
conditions: IF a regulated data class is later routed through a noncompliant channel, compliance risk would need reassessment.
IF either profile is updated with conflicting retention or residency terms, the verdict changes.
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling policies before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are documented.
Review vendor terms for retention and residency.
Record the approved data classes in an operator checklist.
